text:
incident-bot: ALERT 2112349000 1:12 UTC 1:12: DNS anomalies detected for us-central2 endpoints. Symptom: sudden increase in 502/503 and TCP resets to inference frontends. Auto-traffic-shift attempted and partially succeeded but unhealthy failover observed. Paging @emma-oncall and @fred-netops.

emma-oncall: hitting the page, looking at the graph. start 21:10 UTC spike to ~22% 5xx on generate-text in us-central2. Global error rate up ~3%.

fred-netops: I'm seeing lots of duplicate IPs in our edge LB logs. Seems like resolver caches (internal and public) are returning old NLB IPs from an AZ that is being ejected by the provider. Traceroute shows asymmetry: some clients go to healthy AZ, others stick to ejected AZ with packet loss.

gina-sre: Runtime logs show `connection reset by peer` and `http2 stream aborted` around 21:11-21:14. Healthchecks intermittently pass, probably because TCP established then reset mid-request.

infra-bot: automated action: attempted gradual traffic shift 10% -> 50% to us-west2 at 21:13 by policy 'auto-failover-regional'. Canary failed at 30% due to increased latency and 5xx in target.

emma-oncall: immediate mitigation: pause automated policy, start manual hold. Plan: 1) Flush authoritative DNS entries in provider (Route53) 2) Invalidate our CDN resolver caches 3) Force LB connection teardown for problematic AZ endpoints 4) Start a controlled shift to us-west2 with prewarm.

fred-netops: kicked off DNS invalidation: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://invalidate.json` and sent purge to CDN partner. Also asked provider to decommission the problematic AZ interface so caches re-resolve.

gina-sre: Prewarm note: if we shift quickly we'll trigger model reloads and KV cache misses. Starting prewarm: `redwood capacity set --region us-west2 --prewarm 8 --model default`

emma-oncall: Starting forced drain on the sticky AZ: `kubectl label nodes az=us-central2-azb cordon=true && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l az=us-central2-azb`

hannah-cs: Customer impact: ~5.2k failed reqs/min at peak, several enterprise customers reported resumed failures after retries. Notified top 10 affected accounts with temporary workaround: exponential backoff + jitter.

fred-netops: Provider update: they see a control-plane event in us-central2 that ejected a subset of compute from the fabric, but their flow state persisted causing client stickiness. They've applied a fix but we need to force clients to re-resolve NLB IPs. I've lowered our TTLs to 30s and pushed a SOA refresh.

gina-sre: After TTL change + CDN purge we see gradual fall in traffic to bad AZ. However some long-lived TCP keepalives still route there from existing clients. Need to forcibly reset LB connections. Command used: `nc -zv <lb-ip> 443` to detect, then `curl -X POST https://lb-api/force-reset --data '{"ip":"x.x.x.x"}'` (internal tool).

emma-oncall: Executed LB connection teardown for 4 IPs at 21:27. Automated monitors looking for 5xx > 8% or p90 latency > 650ms.

infra-bot: automation: after forced teardown, re-evaluating canary. Manual traffic-shift to us-west2: 25% at 21:29.

gina-sre: Prewarm succeeded, KV cache hit improved from 58% -> 75% after adding instances. Errors in target region stayed low. But we observed a small regression in answer quality for a model variant mismatch on canary (latency ok, but subtle output differences). Reverted that route to ensure model parity.

hannah-cs: CS update sent to customers at 21:35: we explained temporary regional routing issue, suggested retry/backoff and noted no data loss. Opening support tickets for customers that saw degraded outputs.

sre-manager: Note for post-incident: ensure our canary pipeline validates model variant parity before shifting user traffic; also add a forced TCP teardown step to our failover runbook.

emma-oncall: Monitoring shows steady improvement. us-central2 error rate down to 2% at 21:40. Holding at 40% shifted traffic to us-west2 to reduce blast radius while provider fully reconverges.

fred-netops: Running pcap captures from LB edge and selected frontend instances; saving to /var/incidents/2112349000/pcaps/. Collected provider BGP/peering logs and route tables. Opened provider ticket #CEN-211234.

gina-sre: We've queued a follow-up job to warm KV cache further during low-traffic window. Also scheduling a runbook change to increase healthcheck probe frequency during region failovers to catch mid-stream resets.

emma-oncall: Handoff: @fred-netops continues network follow-up, @gina-sre will own runtime warm-up automation and model parity checks, @hannah-cs will continue customer comms. I'll hand to night oncall in 1.5h. Current status: Incident 2112349000 moved to MONITORING. Global error rate back to baseline ~0.3%.

incident-bot: Incident 2112349000: transitioned to MONITORING by emma-oncall at 2112349800. Please file postmortem and tag owners.

hannah-cs: Logged all customer reports in internal tracker under incident 2112349000. CS follow-ups assigned.

sre-manager: Preliminary actions: 1) Add DNS flush + TCP teardown to automated failover playbook; 2) Run DR exercise simulating AZ ejection; 3) Add pre-shift model parity check; 4) Improve TTL handling and CDN purge automation.

emma-oncall: Closing slack thread, moving detailed logs and captures to the incident doc. Thanks team :thumbsup:
